# Jubilees Chapter 18 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** The Binding of Isaac; The Angel Intervenes; Mastema Shamed; Annual Commemoration

---

**18:1** It came to pass in the seventh week, in the first year thereof, in the first month of this jubilee, on the twelfth of that month, that the word of the LORD came to Abraham saying: "Abraham, Abraham." And he said: "Here I am."

**18:2** He said: "Take your son, your only son whom you love — Isaac — and go to the high land, and offer him on one of the mountains that I will tell you."

**18:3** Abraham rose early in the morning, saddled his donkey, took two of his servants with him and Isaac his son, split the wood for the burnt offering, and set out, traveling to the place on the third day.

**18:4** Abraham lifted up his eyes and saw the place from afar.

**18:5** Abraham said to his servants: "Stay here with the donkey; the boy and I will go over there and worship, and we will come back to you."

**18:6** Abraham took the wood for the burnt offering and put it on Isaac his son; and he took the fire and the knife in his hand, and the two of them walked on together.

**18:7** Isaac spoke to his father Abraham and said: "Father!" He said: "Here I am, my son." He said: "Behold the fire and the wood, but where is the lamb for the burnt offering?"

**18:8** Abraham said: "God will provide himself a lamb for the burnt offering, my son." So the two of them walked on together.

**18:9** They came to the place God had told him; Abraham built the altar there, arranged the wood, bound Isaac his son, and laid him on the altar upon the wood.

**18:10** Abraham stretched out his hand and took the knife to slay his son.

**18:11** And I called to him from heaven and said: "Abraham, Abraham." He said: "Here I am."

**18:12** And I said to him: "Do not lay your hand on the boy; do nothing to him, for now I know that you fear God, seeing you have not withheld your son, your only son, from me."

**18:13** Abraham lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, behind him was a ram caught in a thicket by its horns. Abraham went and took the ram and offered it as a burnt offering in place of his son.

**18:14** Abraham called the name of that place "The LORD will provide," as it is said to this day: "In the mount of the LORD it shall be seen."

**18:15** The angel of the LORD called to Abraham from heaven a second time and said: "By myself I have sworn, declares the LORD, because you have done this thing and have not withheld your son, your only son:"

**18:16** "I will surely bless you, and I will surely multiply your descendants like the stars of the sky and like the sand on the seashore; and your descendants shall possess the gate of their enemies."

**18:17** "And in your descendants all the nations of the earth shall be blessed, because you have obeyed my voice."

**18:18** Abraham returned to his servants, and they set out and went together to Beersheba, and Abraham settled at Beersheba.

**18:19** Every year he came back there and built an altar at the place where he had first built one, and called on the name of the LORD: "The LORD, the everlasting God."

**18:20** And he observed that festival with joy each year on that mountain for seven days — eating and drinking and blessing the LORD God who had chosen him and led him out from Ur of the Chaldees, and who had established his covenant with him.

**18:21** When the prince Mastema saw all this, he was put to shame. And Abraham continued to be perfect in all his deeds before the LORD, and his name was honored before the LORD all the days of his life.

**18:22** For in all the temptations with which the LORD tempted him, he was found faithful. His soul loved God and clung to him; he was not slow to act, and his soul was not impatient, because he loved God.

---
*SOPHIA notes: Consensus follows LOGOS throughout. The angel-narrator's first-person at the climax (vv.11-12) preserved as structurally essential to Jubilees. "The LORD, the everlasting God" (v.19) retained as divine title. Mastema's shame (v.21) preserved as the theological resolution of the Job-parallel.*
